verdict: Section 5 holds against direct forgery (reader->admin, single-admin escape, authority raising a bit, authority adopting an orphan, replayed kicks) - every such sequence hits A2/A3/A4/C2/G2/R1/R6 as intended. It does not hold against six indirect sequences that use only rule-compliant records: (1) the only add-reader flow (6.2 ResolveIdentity) lets a compromised node pick the key an admin signs in, so every replica accepts a hostile reader with a valid admin signature; (2) an admin that rotates itself out chooses and keeps M_new while the chain says it is gone; (3) a re-genesis under a known name is accepted by any replica without a pin, including after the reset the spec prescribes; (4) S2 is evaluated outside the lock, so RemoveIdentity can race an admin rewrap and leave a removed key in a head ACL that replicas serve; (5) R6's authority-carry exception has no mode guard, so a mode-A server may revoke a reader without rotating and every verifier accepts it; (6) S2 as written refuses every recovery that replaces authority or backup, i.e. the recovery path cannot do the two things 6.4 introduces it for. Four minor items follow (kick/recovery stalling, recovery staging gate, irreversible backup hijack, SubmitEpoch existence oracle). Fixes are all local rule additions; the architecture stands. Findings file: /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-dragan-fables-for-robots-secret-bunker-iroh/0c07f4bd-a1ff-4066-aa31-2b8de0a5ded7/scratchpad/review/authz-A.json

findings.title: ResolveIdentity lets a compromised node choose the key an admin signs into the ACL; every replica accepts the resulting reader
findings.detail: The chain speaks keys, but the only add-reader flow the spec defines resolves a *name* through the server. Sequence, mode A, head h_n of prod = {alice: rwa}: (1) the compromised node sets identity row 'ci'.endpoint_id = K_att, or simply answers ResolveIdentity with K_att (the registry is server-local; ResolveIdentity is server code). (2) alice runs `client grant --group prod --identity ci --perms r` -> ResolveIdentity{prod,'ci'} -> IdentityId{K_att}. (3) alice's client builds rec n+1: kind=rewrap, acl = head.acl + (K_att, r), wraps to {alice, K_att, authority, backup} with fresh r_i, proof, dek_commit == head's, author=alice, sig alice. (4) Server: S1 ok, S2 ok (K_att is 'registered'), E/C/R/A/G ok. Every replica: C2 ok, C3 ok, A2 ok (alice admin in head.acl), R1 ok, R3 ok, R5 ok, G1/G2 ok - nothing fires; P5 mirrors K_att as reader and every replica serves prod to K_att. Success criterion 4 ('a compromised authoritative node cannot make a replica accept a new reader') is defeated through the spec's own grant flow with one routine admin action. 7.4 lists 'lie about names' as a residual capability but does not draw this consequence, and 6.2 contains no verification step. The k8s operator case is the realistic one: the operator's key is exactly what an admin grants by name.
findings.fix: Make the key, not the name, the thing the admin confirms: `client grant` prints the full resolved EndpointId and requires either `--expect-id <hex>` or an interactive fingerprint confirmation against an out-of-band source (the operator chart already knows its own id; identities can publish theirs); allow `--endpoint-id` directly and treat ResolveIdentity as a convenience only. Optionally add an admin-signed name attestation (name, id) inside the record so auditors and replicas can see name->key bindings and detect a swap. State the residual in 7.4 explicitly.

findings.section: 5 G5 / R6 / A2 (no author-is-recipient rule) / D6 / 7.4 'Stolen SQLite'
findings.title: An admin that rotates itself out chooses and keeps M_new; the chain claims it was rotated away
findings.detail: No rule requires the author of a rotate to be a recipient of it, and G5 explicitly allows an admin to 'remove itself'. Sequence, mode A, head h_n = {alice: rwa, bob: rwa}: alice authors rec n+1: kind=rotate, dek_gen = head+1, acl = {bob: rwa}, wraps = {bob, authority, backup}, fresh dek_commit, reencrypted = digest of every version re-encrypted under DEK_new, author=alice, sig alice. A2 ok (alice admin in head.acl), G2 ok (bob remains), R6 ok (removal is a rotate), R1 ok (alice is not a recipient so no wrap), R2/R3/R5 ok, S1 ok (alice's connection), S4/S5 ok (alice staged the set). `client grant --identity alice --perms 0` is exactly this path (section 11: 'losing read -> 6.1'). Every verifier accepts and `client epoch log` prints 'alice rotate gen k -alice(r)'. But alice drew M_new in 3.3 step 1 and holds DEK_new; every later Put stays under gen k until someone *else* rotates, so alice reads all future writes from any later copy of either database. 7.4 'Stolen SQLite: readable only by keys in the current record's wraps' and D6 'makes a kicked reader's old wraps protect nothing' are false for the author, and no auditor can tell from the chain. Same for rwa -> w (G1 forces admin off with read, still legal under G5).
findings.fix: Add A5: for kind = rotate, `author in recipients(rec)` (for recovery this is automatic - backup is always pinned; for the authority in mode A likewise). An admin that wants out is kicked by another admin (D5 already allows admin-kicks-admin) or drops only its admin/write bits with a carry and is then kicked; G2 already stops the last admin leaving. Reword G5 to drop 'remove itself', and make `client grant --identity <self> --perms 0` fail with that explanation. Note in 7.4 that a departing admin must be rotated out by someone else.

findings.section: 5 C1 / 10 P1-P2 (TOFU) / P4 reset / D9 / 13 e2e (3)
findings.title: Re-genesis under a known name is accepted by every replica that has no pin - fresh replicas and any replica after the reset the spec prescribes
findings.detail: Genesis is the one record the online key alone may author (A1), and C1/P1 protect only a verifier that already holds a pin for the name. Sequence: the compromised node holds operational.key and, in mode A, prod's DEK (its authority wrap). It mints genesis': group_id' fresh, name='prod', mode A, authority/backup unchanged, acl={K_att: rwa}, wraps to {K_att, authority, backup}, proof, reencrypted over prod's versions re-encrypted under M', signed by the authority. A1 ok, C1 ok for any verifier with no head for group_id' and no pin for 'prod', E/R/G ok, P2 with `expect_keys` ok (same keys). It serves genesis' + prod's re-encrypted ciphertext under name 'prod'. Every replica that lacks a pin accepts it as `sync-genesis-tofu` and serves prod to K_att: (a) a newly provisioned replica or k8s operator, (b) a replica after `db drop-group --group prod` / `Replica::reset_group` - the reset P4/D9 tell the operator to run after a rewind, which the node can provoke by first serving a rewound chain, (c) a replica whose mirror was lost. Test 13(3) ('re-presents a known name under a new genesis -> the replica rejects') is true only for pinned replicas. Success criterion 4 fails for every replica in the window, and nothing in section 5 or 10 fires.
findings.fix: Give replicas an out-of-band genesis pin: chart value `bunker.expectGenesis: {prod: <genesis_hash>}` / `ReplicaBuilder::expect_genesis`, and make `reset_group` take the new expected genesis hash instead of clearing the pin; make TOFU opt-in (`--tofu`) and emit `EpochRejected{reason: unpinned-genesis}` otherwise. Alternatively require genesis to be co-signed by the backup key (a second signature field) so the online key alone cannot mint a trusted root; CreateGroup would then need an offline step, which argues for the pin approach. Say in 7.4 that a compromised node can seed any un-pinned replica with any roster.

findings.section: 5 S2 / S8 / 6.1 server commit / 6.3 revoked list / 10 P5 / S7
findings.title: RemoveIdentity races an admin's rewrap (S2 is evaluated outside the lock): a removed key ends up in a head ACL with a valid wrap and replicas serve it
findings.detail: 6.1: 'S1-S2 and E/C/R/A/G ... all outside the lock (S8); then under the lock: S3 CAS; S4; install'. Sequence, mode A, head h_n of prod = {alice: rwa}; bob is registered with no row on prod. t1: alice submits rec n+1 = rewrap adding (bob, r), wraps {alice, bob, authority, backup}; the server runs S2 outside the lock - bob is registered, ok. t2: a service admin runs RemoveIdentity(bob): identity row deleted; bob had no row on prod so no server record is authored for prod, head stays h_n; `revoked` is not written (6.3 populates it only for ids that sit in a head at removal time, and only 'mode E, until the rotate'). t3: alice's submit takes the lock: S3 ok (head still h_n), install. Result: bob's key is prod's head reader with a valid wrap. The authoritative node denies bob at the transport (no identity row) - though `AddIdentity{revive:true}` (S7) would silently restore full access - but every replica applies P5: mirrored ACL = head ACL minus `revoked` = includes bob; bob `Get`s prod from every replica (shown as hex, absent from `names`). In mode A the spec relies on RemoveIdentity's rotate to make the key harmless; no rotate covers prod. Nothing in section 5 fires because S2 was true when evaluated. The same window exists for any id in rec.acl \ head.acl.
findings.fix: Re-evaluate S2 for every id in rec.acl \ head.acl inside the install transaction (one query per added id, cheap). Independently, define `revoked` as 'any head-ACL id absent from the registry', maintained at RemoveIdentity *and* at every install, in all modes - then P5 protects replicas even if a race slips through - and have the server author a shrink for such ids. Rewrite the 6.3 sentence about 'a removed id that still appears in a head' to name this as the only way the state arises.

findings.section: 5 R6 (authority-carry exception) / A3 / 6.3 legacy Grant / 4.1 kinds table
findings.title: Authority carry that removes a reader is legal in mode A: revocation without rotation, accepted by every verifier, with needs_rotation undefined for mode A
findings.detail: R6 allows 'kind = carry with author = authority' whenever a recipient is removed, with no mode guard; A3 lists carry and rotate for the authority and does not say which applies when; 6.3 says a legacy Grant shrink is 'authored by the authority as carry/rotate per A3'. Sequence, mode A, head h_n = {alice: rwa, bob: r}: alice sends legacy Grant{prod, bob, perms: 0}; the server authors rec n+1: kind=carry, acl={alice: rwa}, wraps = head.wraps minus bob's entry (byte-identical subset), n_s=0, proof_e=0, dek_gen/dek_commit unchanged, reencrypted=0, author=authority. R4 ok, R1 ok, R6 ok (carry by authority), A3 ok (shrink), G2 ok, C4 ok. Server and every replica accept. bob keeps M; the server keeps serving Put under the same generation (the needs_rotation write fence in 6.3/7.2 is specified for mode E only), so every future write is readable by bob from any later copy of either database. Today's code always rotates when read is lost (`revoke_read_and_rotate`, `remove_identity_with_rotations`); the new rules let a compliant mode-A server regress and let replicas verify the regression as valid. RemoveIdentity in mode A could be implemented the same way with the same acceptance. 7.4 'Compromised reader key: after the rotate nothing in the database is under a generation it knew' presumes a rotate that R6 does not require.
findings.fix: R6: '... or kind = carry with author = authority **and mode == E**'. A3/6.3: in mode A an authority record that removes a recipient MUST be a rotate (RemoveIdentity, legacy Grant losing read); carry is for w/a-only shrinks. Define needs_rotation as a mode-E state only, or specify the mode-A Put fence too. Add a verifier test: authority carry removing a reader in mode A is rejected.

findings.section: 5 S2 ('configured authority/backup ids equal the record's') vs C4 / A4 / 6.4 / 12.3 / S4-S5
findings.title: S2 refuses every recovery that replaces authority or backup - the two things 6.4 introduces recovery for - and the old-key-less server cannot install one anyway
findings.detail: Sequence, operational-key compromise, mode A: the operator authors rec n+1 = recovery with authority=K_new, backup unchanged, rotate branch (R6: the old authority is a removed recipient), signed by the backup key, and any registered identity submits it while 'the service is never stopped' (6.4). C4 ok (recovery exempt), A4 ok, R6 ok, R1 ok - then S2: 'The configured authority/backup ids equal the record's (also for genesis)'; the running server's configured authority is K_old != K_new -> Failed. `--backup <id>` and `--mode` fail S2 the same way. If the operator instead restarts the server with K_new first: 12.3 says `read_secret` opens the head record's authority wrap, which is addressed to K_old, so reads fail; S5 'decrypts the row it replaces under the old DEK' and S4 'stragglers are re-encrypted by the server itself' need the old DEK, which K_new cannot open - so the recovery is verifiable but not installable under S4/S5 as written. The recovery path therefore does strictly less than 6.4 and 7.4 ('Replaced by a recovery record') claim; the only working case is a recovery that changes nothing pinned.
findings.fix: For kind = recovery, S2 compares authority/backup to the *head* (C4 already guarantees that for other kinds) and the install transaction adopts the record's authority/backup/mode into `meta`. Specify the operational-key replacement procedure: the server is restarted with both keys (old for S4/S5 against the old head, new for the new head's wrap), or during a mode-A recovery stragglers answer StaleVersions and S5's old-DEK decryption is done with the old key if present and skipped (digest-only) otherwise; backup replacement needs only the meta update. Add a server test: recovery replacing authority installs and the next Get works under K_new.

findings.section: 6.1 step 8 / S6 / G5 / C2 / 6.4 trigger 'rogue admin'
findings.title: A kick target (or rogue admin) stalls kicks and offline recoveries indefinitely with valid self-w-bit carries
findings.detail: Sequence, head h_n = {alice: rwa, bob: rwa}: alice exports, re-encrypts and builds a rotate kicking bob against h_n. bob loops: carry n+1 with acl toggling only bob's own write bit (G5 permits; S6 does not fire because the ACL changed; R4/R6/A2 ok). alice's SubmitEpoch -> EpochConflict; 6.1 step 8 refuses to rebase automatically over a record authored by the kick target, so alice restarts manually at step 2 - and loses every time against a loop. A recovery bundle (6.4) built offline against h_n fails C2 the same way and costs another offline ceremony per attempt, so the 'rogue admin locked everyone out' trigger is not recoverable over the wire while the rogue key is live. bob keeps read until a service admin runs RemoveIdentity; the spec never names that as the remedy.
findings.fix: Name RemoveIdentity (server shrink, always wins) as the first step of both flows in 6.1 and 6.4. Refuse admin records that change only the author's own bits (extend S6), or rate-limit records per author. Optionally let the server accept a rotate whose `prev` is an ancestor when every intervening record was authored by an id the rotate removes and touched only that id's bits.

findings.section: 6.4 step 3 / 9 (StageVersions requires admin) / S1 exception / S4
findings.title: Anyone may carry a recovery, but only an admin may stage the re-encrypted set it depends on - an orphaned group's recovery-with-rotate cannot be submitted
findings.detail: A recovery that changes authority (mode A), backup, mode, or removes a reader must be a rotate (R6/G4) and therefore needs a staged set (S4, 'staged like 6.1'). Section 9 gates StageVersions on `admin`. An orphaned group has no admin; in mode A only a service admin's implicit admin can stage, in mode E nobody can. So the exact case 6.4 is introduced for ('orphaned group', 'operational-key replacement') is unsubmittable by the 'any registered identity' S1 promises, and unsubmittable at all in mode E.
findings.fix: Gate StageVersions on 'admin of the group, or presenter of a recovery record for this group that passes E/C/R/A/G against the current head' (send the record with the first StageVersions; key the stage by record hash for recoveries). State in section 9 that service-admin implicit admin covers StageVersions in mode A.

findings.title: One accepted recovery with a stolen backup key re-roots the group permanently; the real backup key has no wire path back
findings.detail: Sequence: the attacker holds backup.key and any registered identity. Submits rec n+1 = recovery, backup=K_att, acl={K_att2: rwa}, rotate. A4 ok (author == head.backup), G2 ok, R6 ok, S2 ok (if fixed per the S2 finding, or once meta is updated). From then on A4 requires K_att; the operator's real backup key can author nothing, the authority is shrink-only (A3), admins cannot touch `backup` (G4). The only remedy is a database restore plus per-replica reset (D9). The old design let the operational key re-wrap to a new backup key; 7.4 says the compromised backup 'authors recoveries' but not that a single accepted recovery is irreversible online.
findings.fix: Either document the restore-and-reset procedure as the only remedy in 6.4/7.4, or require `backup` replacement to be co-signed by the current authority (a second signature field on recovery, verified when `backup` changes), so a stolen backup key alone cannot re-root a group whose server is honest.

findings.section: 5 S1 exception / 5 ordering ('first failing rule rejects') / crypto-design.md section 7 (uniform denial)
findings.title: SubmitEpoch's recovery exception turns its error replies into a group-existence oracle for any registered identity
findings.detail: Any registered identity, even with zero groups, may send SubmitEpoch{group: X, record: bytes with kind=recovery}. For an unknown X the first failing rule is C1 ('no head and not a genesis'); for a known X it is C3 ('bad signature') - distinct `Failed{reason}` strings, and `EpochConflict{head_epoch, head_hash}` if a previously fetched recovery record is replayed. The client protocol's stated property is that denials do not reveal whether a group exists.
findings.fix: For a caller that is not an admin of `group`, answer the uniform `Denied` unless C3 verifies under the group's head.backup, evaluated before any other rule and before any conflict reply; never return EpochConflict or a reason string to a non-admin carrier.
